## Editable network graph powered by Pyodide and D3

This page lets you edit a Python graph script and renders a networkx-style
graph in the browser. It's built around a single `GraphDisplay` class that
owns the graph data and its viewport; the Python editor below and the
button panel next to it are two interchangeable *inputs* that drive that
same display without it ever needing to know which one is in use.

The editor supports a small NetworkX-like API:

- `G = nx.Graph()`
- `G.add_node(name)`
- `G.add_edge(u, v, weight=1)`
- `G.nodes()`
- `G.edges()`
- `G.degree(node)`

```{=html}
<div id="graph-widget-1" class="graph-widget">
  <div class="graph-widget__columns">
    <div class="graph-widget__panel">
      <h3>Edit Python graph code</h3>
      <label for="python-editor-1">Python (uses a small <code>networkx</code>-like <code>nx</code> shim)</label>
      <textarea id="python-editor-1" data-role="python-editor" rows="14">import json

G = nx.Graph()
G.add_edge("Alice", "Bob")
G.add_edge("Bob", "Carol")
G.add_edge("Carol", "Dave")
G.add_edge("Alice", "Dave")
G.add_edge("Bob", "Eve")
G.add_edge("Eve", "Frank")
G.add_edge("Frank", "Carol")

# Optional: inspect or modify the graph
print("nodes:", list(G.nodes()))
print("edges:", list(G.edges()))

# The renderer uses G if graph_output is not defined.
# You can also set graph_output manually to a {"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]} dict.
</textarea>
      <div class="graph-widget__row">
        <button data-role="run-code">Run Python</button>
        <button data-role="reset-code" class="secondary">Reset code</button>
        <button data-role="show-json" class="secondary">Show current JSON</button>
      </div>
      <pre data-role="json-output" class="graph-widget__json" hidden></pre>
      <div data-role="status" class="graph-widget__status"></div>

      <h3>Or drive the same display with buttons</h3>
      <div class="graph-widget__row">
        <label for="adjacent-node-input-1">Node</label>
        <input id="adjacent-node-input-1" type="text" data-role="adjacent-node-input" placeholder="e.g. Bob">
        <button data-role="highlight-adjacent">Highlight adjacent</button>
      </div>
      <div class="graph-widget__row">
        <label for="path-input-1">Path</label>
        <input id="path-input-1" type="text" data-role="path-input" placeholder="Alice,Bob,Eve,Frank">
        <button data-role="traverse-path">Traverse path</button>
      </div>
      <div class="graph-widget__row">
        <label for="add-edge-from-input-1">Edge</label>
        <input id="add-edge-from-input-1" type="text" data-role="add-edge-from-input" placeholder="from">
        <input id="add-edge-to-input-1" type="text" data-role="add-edge-to-input" placeholder="to">
        <button data-role="add-edge">Add edge</button>
      </div>
      <div class="graph-widget__row">
        <button data-role="clear-highlights" class="secondary">Clear highlights</button>
      </div>
      <div data-role="actions-status" class="graph-widget__status"></div>
    </div>

    <div class="graph-widget__output">
      <div class="graph-widget__viewport-container" data-role="viewport-container"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

<!--
  graph-model.js          - pure { nodes, edges } data helpers, no DOM
  graph-display.js        - GraphDisplay: owns graph data + the rendered
                             viewport; add/update/delete node & edge,
                             highlightNode/Edge/Adjacent, traversePath
  graph-display.css       - styling for GraphDisplay's own viewport
  py-graph-engine.js      - Pyodide + the fake `networkx` API, run(code) -> {nodes, edges}
  python-editor-input.js  - an "input step": Python editor -> GraphDisplay
  graph-actions-panel.js  - a second "input step": buttons -> GraphDisplay
  graph-app.js            - composition root: wires the pieces above to one page
  styles.css              - layout/chrome for the demo widget

  Swapping the input mechanism (e.g. a future drag-and-drop UI) means
  writing a new file like python-editor-input.js / graph-actions-panel.js;
  graph-display.js never has to change.

  Another .qmd that only wants the display can import just that piece:

    <script type="module">
      import { GraphDisplay } from "./graph-display.js";
      const display = new GraphDisplay({ d3: window.d3 });
      document.getElementById("some-container").appendChild(display.viewport);
      display.addEdge("Alice", "Bob");
    </script>

  Note: embed-resources: true inlines these local files into the final
  single-file HTML at render time. During `quarto preview`, ES module
  imports require being served over http(s), so use `quarto preview` /
  `quarto render` rather than opening the rendered HTML straight from
  the filesystem (file://).
-->
```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="graph-display.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3@7.9.0/dist/d3.min.js"></script>
<script type="module">
  import { GraphApp } from "./graph-app.js";
  GraphApp.mount(document.getElementById("graph-widget-1"), { d3: window.d3 });
</script>
```
